**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-01 — Reference number POC-B7C7B913DC-54149**
**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Governing policy:** PH Medical Policy 91581-R23 SPINE PROCEDURES (https://priorityhealth.stylelabs.cloud/api/public/content/5f005b3ee3044b68ad920d57974c2d68?v=785108c8), effective 2026-03-01

---

Dear Priority Health Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551). The notice of adverse benefit determination is dated 2026-08-01 and carries reference number POC-B7C7B913DC-54149. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, and that the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has requested and documented as necessary.

## The plan has not identified the criteria it applied

I located the policy the plan names as governing spine procedures, PH Medical Policy 91581-R23 SPINE PROCEDURES. I have read that document in full, and it does not set out medical-necessity criteria for this specific operation. I am therefore not able to quote any plan language back to you, because none that applies to this procedure has been published or shared with me. I want to be clear and accurate on that point rather than attribute requirements to the plan that the plan has not stated.

That matters for this appeal. The denial says my case did not meet the plan's criteria, but I have not been told what those criteria are, which threshold or requirement my records were measured against, or which one the reviewer concluded was not met. Without that, I can only present my full clinical record and ask that it be measured against the actual standard.

**Request for the criteria in writing.** I ask Priority Health to provide me, in writing and at no cost, the complete clinical review criteria that were actually applied to reference number POC-B7C7B913DC-54149 — including the specific criteria set used by TurningPoint, if the review of my request was delegated to TurningPoint, along with the version and the date in effect on 2026-08-01. I understand these criteria may be requested through the form on the policy page for PH Medical Policy 91581-R23 SPINE PROCEDURES or through Priority Health's Prism portal under Authorizations > Authorization Criteria Lookup. The plan, not the patient and not the surgeon, holds these documents. If the criteria are produced and my records fall short of some specific requirement, I ask to be told exactly which one, so that I can respond to it. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in spine surgery.

## What my records actually show

These are the facts documented in the prior authorization packet my surgeon submitted:

- **Duration and course of symptoms.** I have had 18 months of progressive neck pain. It has not been relieved by rest.
- **Supervised conservative treatment.** I completed supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, over 10 weeks from 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21 — 18 visits in all. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trials.** I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-22, which gave me about 4 weeks of partial relief before the symptoms returned.
- **Imaging.** MRI of the cervical spine on 2026-05-20 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.
- **Symptoms and function.** I have radicular pain and numbness going into my right thumb and index finger, with weakness.
- **Examination findings.** My exam shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit that corresponds to the level seen on the MRI.
- **Surgical risk factors.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, my record documents an identified structural cause on imaging, physical examination findings and a neurologic deficit at that same level, symptoms that have continued and worsened over 18 months, and a documented course of supervised therapy, medication, and injection that did not give me lasting relief. My surgeon reviewed all of this and documented that the fusion is the appropriate next step in my care.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Priority Health overturn the denial dated 2026-08-01 and authorize CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. In the alternative, I ask that the plan send me the written criteria described above and reconsider my request against them, identifying any specific requirement the plan believes is unmet.

I understand this is a Level 1 appeal and must be received within 180 days of the adverse determination, by 2027-01-28, as stated in the denial notice. I am submitting it within that period. I understand that Priority Health uses a three-level process — a Level 2 appeal filed within 90 days, and then external review through the State of Michigan within 127 days — and I intend to use those further levels if needed. I am submitting this appeal to Priority Health, Member Appeals, 1231 East Beltline Ave. NE, Grand Rapids, MI 49525-4501; by fax to 616-975-8894; by email to phmemberappeals@priorityhealth.com; or through the online appeal form on priorityhealth.com. I understand a verbal appeal may also be made by calling the number on the back of my membership card.

I am glad to provide any additional records the reviewer needs, and I authorize Dr. Marchetti and my physical therapy provider to release any further documentation on my behalf. Thank you for taking the time to look at my case again.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Mercado**
